Traits evolving by an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with one or several optima

Source: R/traits_ou.R
traits_ou.Rd

Simulates traits along a tree under the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) model of Hansen (1997), with the multi-optimum ("multi-peak") extension of Butler & King (2004). Along each branch the trait is pulled towards the optimum theta of the selective regime of that branch with strength alpha, while drifting with rate sigma2. Values are drawn exactly from the transition distribution of the process: over a branch of length t, a trait with value x at the start has, at the end, a normal distribution with mean theta + (x - theta) * exp(-alpha * t) and variance sigma2 / (2 * alpha) * (1 - exp(-2 * alpha * t)).

Usage

traits_ou(
  tree,
  n_traits = 1,
  alpha = 0,
  sigma2 = 1,
  theta = 0,
  regimes = NULL,
  root = 0
)

Arguments

tree

A rooted phylo tree with branch lengths.

n_traits

Number of independent traits.

alpha

Strength of selection towards the optimum (0 = Brownian motion).

sigma2

Rate of the stochastic (drift) component.

theta

Optimum of each regime: one value for a single optimum, or a named vector with one value per regime (names as in regimes).

regimes

Selective regime of each branch, in the order of the edges of tree reordered "cladewise" (ape::reorder.phylo(tree, "cladewise")), as returned by paint_regimes(). NULL puts every branch in one regime.

root

Trait value at the root.

Value

Matrix with one row per tip (tip labels as row names) and one column per trait.

Details

With alpha = 0 the process is Brownian motion with rate sigma2, and the optima play no role. Each branch belongs to a single regime, so a shift in optimum happens at the start of the branch where the regime changes.

References

Butler, M. A., & King, A. A. (2004). Phylogenetic comparative analysis: a modeling approach for adaptive evolution. The American Naturalist, 164, 683–695. doi:10.1086/426002

Hansen, T. F. (1997). Stabilizing selection and the comparative analysis of adaptation. Evolution, 51, 1341–1351. doi:10.1111/j.1558-5646.1997.tb01457.x

See also

paint_regimes() to assign regimes to clades.

Examples

set.seed(1)
tr <- ape::rcoal(20)
# Brownian motion
traits_ou(tr, alpha = 0)[1:3, ]
#>        t8        t7       t11 
#> 0.7324355 1.0476049 0.6082487 
# two optima: the clade of node 25 evolves towards 10, the rest towards 0
reg <- paint_regimes(tr, nodes = 25)
x <- traits_ou(tr, alpha = 2, theta = c(`0` = 0, `1` = 10), regimes = reg)
round(x[, 1], 1)
#>   t8   t7  t11  t17   t4  t13  t20   t9  t15  t19  t16  t18   t5  t14  t10  t12 
#>  0.5  0.5  0.6  0.7  0.6  0.4  6.8  6.9  0.8  0.1  0.5 -0.3 -0.3 -0.3  0.0  0.2 
#>   t6   t1   t3   t2 
#>  0.2  0.3 -0.1 -0.2
